# 什么是 Google-Extended？

- 原标题：What Is Google-Extended?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/google-extended/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

Google-Extended 是 robots.txt 中的控制标识，而不是一个独立爬虫。发布者用它决定自己的内容能否用于训练 Google 的 Gemini 模型，以及为模型提供依据约束。它没有独立的用户代理字符串，因为 Google 使用现有代理进行抓取；屏蔽它不会影响 Google 搜索的收录或排名。

### 关键要点

- Google-Extended 是可以放入 robots.txt 的独立产品标识。按照 Google 的文档，它“没有独立的 HTTP 请求用户代理字符串。抓取通过现有 Google 用户代理字符串进行”。
- 它控制内容能否用于训练支撑 Gemini Apps 和 Vertex AI API 的 Gemini 模型，以及为这些模型提供依据约束；除此之外不控制其他用途。
- Google 表示，Google-Extended“不会影响网站是否被纳入 Google 搜索，也不会被用作 Google 搜索的排名信号”。
- Google 于 2023 年 9 月 28 日，在《网页发布者控制功能更新》公告中推出 Google-Extended。

### Google-Extended 如何运作

在人们归入 [AI 爬虫](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/)的那些标识中，Google-Extended 是个异类。GPTBot、ClaudeBot 和 PerplexityBot 都是真实的机器人程序：它们通过 HTTP 请求页面，并在 `User-Agent` 请求头中标明身份。Google-Extended 不是。Google 的文档明确表示，它“没有独立的 HTTP 请求用户代理字符串。抓取通过现有 Google 用户代理字符串进行”。你不会在服务器日志中看到“Google-Extended”，因为从来没有一个叫这个名字的程序来敲门。

Google-Extended 实际上是一个*控制标识*：你可以在 robots.txt 中指向这个名称，以表达一项许可。当 Google 读到 `User-agent: Google-Extended`，后面接着 `Disallow: /` 时，并不会停止抓取网站；Googlebot 仍然会为搜索进行收录。变化的是 Google 已经取得的内容可以如何*被使用*：禁止规则告诉 Google，不要将页面用于 Gemini 模型的训练和依据约束。抓取与使用被分开，这就是该设计的重点。

正是这种分离，使屏蔽 Google-Extended 不会带来 SEO 惩罚，也让它更适合被理解为许可决策，而不是技术决策。

### Google-Extended 管理哪些用途

Google-Extended 的范围被有意设定得很窄。按照 Google 的文档，它控制内容能否用于训练以下两类产品背后的生成式模型，并为其提供依据约束：

- **Gemini Apps**：面向消费者的 Gemini 助手及其未来几代模型。
- **Vertex AI API for Gemini**：Google 的企业级生成式 AI 平台。

它也明确排除了一些用途。Google 表示，Google-Extended“不会影响网站是否被纳入 Google 搜索，也不会被用作 Google 搜索的排名信号”。尤其需要注意，它与搜索内部支持 [AI 概览](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/)的依据约束是不同的控制项；Google-Extended 面向的是 Gemini 的训练和依据约束，而不是你在搜索结果中的展示。由于设置方式与其他标识相同，它可以自然地纳入更广泛的 [AI 机器人屏蔽](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-bot-blocking/)政策或 [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/) 声明，与针对 [GPTBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/gptbot/)、[ClaudeBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/claudebot/) 和 [PerplexityBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/perplexitybot/) 的逐个机器人规则并列。

### Google-Extended 示例

Google-Extended 的起源本身，就是理解其用途最清晰的实例。**2023 年 9 月 28 日**，Google 在题为《网页发布者控制功能更新》的文章中宣布推出它。公告的表述明确说明了其意图：Google-Extended 被作为“一项新的控制功能”引入，让网页发布者“管理其网站是否帮助改进”Google 的生成式 API，“包括为这些产品提供支持的未来几代模型”；这一控制独立于 Google 搜索，而且不影响网站在搜索中的出现。

这次发布之所以重要，是因为它确立了其他服务提供商随后沿用的模板。在 Google-Extended 之前，发布者唯一粗放的控制手段，是完全屏蔽 Googlebot；那样为了避免 AI 训练，也会毁掉自己的搜索可见度。Google-Extended 把两者解耦：保留搜索抓取，同时退出 AI 用途。Google 明确将通过 robots.txt 提供“简单且可扩展的控制方式”称为“重要的一步”，并认为“所有 AI 模型提供商都应该提供”这样的控制。如今，这种设计已成为常态，但 2023 年 9 月的公告仍然是原始记录，说明它要消除的取舍：保留可见度，而不被迫参与模型训练。

### 人们容易弄错的一点

我每次都需要帮团队消除的担忧是：“如果屏蔽 Google-Extended，我会从 Google 消失吗？”不会。这是 Google 特意与搜索解耦的一项 AI 控制标识。Google-Extended 甚至不是爬虫，而是一条规则，用来管理已抓取的内容可以如何*被使用*于 Gemini 训练和依据约束。Googlebot 仍然会像以前一样收录你，排名不会因此变化。禁止它所放弃的，只是让页面为未来 Gemini 模型提供内容。把它当成内容许可决策，而不是 SEO 决策，选择就清晰得多。

### 常见问题

#### 什么是 Google-Extended？

Google-Extended 是 robots.txt 中的一个标识，让发布者控制 Google 能否使用其内容训练 Gemini AI 模型，以及为其提供依据约束。它不是具有独立用户代理字符串的爬虫，而是 Google 在读取 robots.txt 时遵守的一种使用控制信号。

#### 屏蔽 Google-Extended 会损害我的 Google 搜索排名吗？

不会。Google 明确表示，Google-Extended 不影响 Google 搜索收录，也不是排名信号。屏蔽它，只会让内容退出 Gemini 模型的训练和依据约束用途。Googlebot 仍会正常抓取并收录网站。

#### 如何屏蔽 Google-Extended？

在 robots.txt 中添加 `User-agent: Google-Extended`，然后写 `Disallow: /`。由于 Google-Extended 没有独立爬虫，这条规则是在告诉 Google，不要将已经抓取的内容用于 Gemini 训练或依据约束，而不会改变 Googlebot 为搜索收录页面的方式。

#### Google-Extended 实际控制什么？

它控制你的内容能否帮助训练为 Gemini Apps 和 Vertex AI API for Gemini 提供支持的 Gemini 模型，以及为这些模型提供依据约束。它不会影响搜索、广告系统或这一生成式 AI 用途之外的任何产品。

### 核心结论

Google-Extended 是通过 robots.txt 表达的一项使用许可，不是你能在日志里找到的机器人。它回答一个问题：Google 能否用你的内容训练 Gemini，并为其提供依据约束？同时，它有意不触及搜索。禁止它是一项不会带来排名代价的内容许可选择，因此，它既是发布者能设置的风险最低的 AI 控制之一，也是最容易被误解的控制之一。

## 英文原文

Google-Extended is a robots.txt control token, not a distinct crawler. Publishers use it to decide whether their content may be used to train and ground Google’s Gemini models. It has no separate user-agent string — Google crawls with existing agents — and blocking it does not affect Google Search indexing or ranking.

### Key Takeaways

- Google-Extended is a standalone product token you place in robots.txt; per Google’s documentation it “doesn’t have a separate HTTP request user agent string. Crawling is done with existing Google user agent strings.”
- It controls whether content may be used to train and ground Gemini models that power Gemini Apps and the Vertex AI API — nothing else.
- Google states Google-Extended “does not impact a site’s inclusion in Google Search nor is it used as a ranking signal in Google Search.”
- Google introduced Google-Extended on September 28, 2023, in its “An update on web publisher controls” announcement.

### How Google-Extended Works

Google-Extended is the odd one out among the tokens people group with [AI crawlers](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/). GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are actual bots — programs that request your pages over HTTP and identify themselves in the `User-Agent` header. Google-Extended is not. Google’s documentation is explicit: it “doesn’t have a separate HTTP request user agent string. Crawling is done with existing Google user agent strings.” You will never see “Google-Extended” in your server logs, because nothing by that name ever knocks on your door.

Instead, Google-Extended is a *control token* — a name you can address in robots.txt to express a permission. When Google reads `User-agent: Google-Extended` followed by `Disallow: /`, it does not stop crawling your site; Googlebot keeps indexing you for Search. What changes is how the content Google already has may be *used*: a disallow rule tells Google not to feed your pages into training and grounding for its Gemini models. The crawling and the usage are separated, which is the whole point of the design.

That separation is why blocking Google-Extended carries no SEO penalty, and why it is best understood as a licensing decision rather than a technical one.

### What Google-Extended Governs

Google-Extended has a deliberately narrow scope. Per Google’s documentation, it controls whether content may be used to train and ground the generative models behind two products:

- **Gemini Apps** — the consumer-facing Gemini assistant and its future model generations.
- **Vertex AI API for Gemini** — Google’s enterprise generative-AI platform.

And it has an equally explicit exclusion. Google states that Google-Extended “does not impact a site’s inclusion in Google Search nor is it used as a ranking signal in Google Search.” Notably, it is a separate lever from the grounding that powers [AI Overviews](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/) inside Search itself — Google-Extended targets Gemini training and grounding, not your appearance in Search results. Because it is set the same way as every other token, it fits naturally into a broader [AI bot blocking](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-bot-blocking/) policy or an [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/) declaration, sitting alongside per-bot rules for [GPTBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/gptbot/), [ClaudeBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/claudebot/), and [PerplexityBot](https://roborank.io/glossary/perplexitybot/).

### Example of Google-Extended

Google-Extended’s origin is itself the clearest worked example of what it is for. On **September 28, 2023**, Google announced it in a post titled “An update on web publisher controls.” The framing in that announcement is the definitive statement of intent: Google-Extended was introduced as “a new control” letting web publishers “manage whether their sites help improve” Google’s generative APIs, “including future generations of models that power” those products — separate from and without affecting their presence in Google Search.

That launch matters because it set the template every other provider followed. Before Google-Extended, a publisher’s only blunt instrument was blocking Googlebot entirely — which would have destroyed their Search visibility to avoid AI training. Google-Extended decoupled the two: keep the Search crawl, opt out of the AI use. Google explicitly called making “simple and scalable controls” available through robots.txt “an important step” it believed “all providers of AI models should make available.” The design has since become the norm, but the September 2023 announcement is the primary record of the trade-off it was built to eliminate — visibility without conscription into model training.

### The thing people get wrong

The fear I have to talk teams out of, every single time, is "if I block Google-Extended, will I disappear from Google?" No. This is the one AI-control token Google went out of its way to decouple from Search. Google-Extended isn’t even a crawler — it’s a rule that governs how already-crawled content may be *used* for Gemini training and grounding. Googlebot still indexes you exactly as before; your rankings don’t move. The only thing you give up by disallowing it is having your pages feed future Gemini models. Treat that as a licensing decision, not an SEO one, and the choice gets a lot clearer.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is Google-Extended?

Google-Extended is a robots.txt token that lets publishers control whether Google can use their content to train and ground its Gemini AI models. It is not a crawler with its own user-agent string; it is a usage-control signal Google honors when reading robots.txt.

#### Does blocking Google-Extended hurt my Google Search rankings?

No. Google explicitly states Google-Extended does not affect inclusion in Google Search and is not a ranking signal. Blocking it only opts your content out of training and grounding Gemini models. Googlebot continues to crawl and index your site normally.

#### How do I block Google-Extended?

Add `User-agent: Google-Extended` then `Disallow: /` to your robots.txt. Because Google-Extended has no separate crawler, this rule tells Google not to use crawled content for Gemini training or grounding, without changing how Googlebot indexes your pages for Search.

#### What does Google-Extended actually control?

It controls whether your content may help train and ground the Gemini models that power Gemini Apps and the Vertex AI API for Gemini. It does not touch Search, ad systems, or any product outside that generative-AI use case.

### The Bottom Line

Google-Extended is a usage permission expressed in robots.txt, not a bot you can catch in your logs. It answers one question — may Google use your content to train and ground Gemini? — and deliberately leaves Search untouched. Disallowing it is a content-licensing choice with zero ranking cost, which is what makes it the least risky and most misunderstood AI control a publisher can set.
